hypothesis: Short EURGBP when the close is >= +2 sigma above its 50-day MA has positive NET expectancy after spread and swap, over a hold of 10-20 trading days.
rationale: Descriptive z>=+2 bucket: mean 20d forward move -189 pips gross (n=70, 10y), and 65.7% of days sit within +-2% of MA200. Mean reversion is the mechanism (Hurst 0.358, VR60 0.516).
iv: z-score of (close - MA50) / sd(close - MA50), measured on the close that is fully available before entry
dv: net pips per trade: (entry_fill - exit_fill) minus round-trip cost
entry_rule: ENTER_SHORT if z >= +2.0 at bar close T. Fill at T+1 open (or limit at T close + 0.15*ATR buffer). One position at a time.
exit_rule: Exit at the earlier of: close crossing MA50, or 20 trading days elapsed (time stop). Hard stop loss at entry + 3.0 * ATR(20).
cost_assumption: spread 0.9 pip round trip (Dukascopy median, measured) + swap/financing per night (BROKER SPEC MISSING -> use 0.0 and 0.3 pip/night as bounds)
null_hypothesis: Net expectancy <= 0 after cost, i.e. the apparent reversion is drift, cost, or in-sample selection.
rejection_criteria: Reject if: (a) net expectancy <= 0 on validation block, OR (b) block-bootstrap 95% CI of net expectancy includes 0, OR (c) all profit comes from <= 5 trades, OR (d) effect vanishes in the locked OOS block.
sample_requirement: >= 30 independent entries in-sample (10y has ~70 -> OK); >= 10 in each validation block; if fewer, extend history via broker MT5 export before testing.
validation_design: IS 2016-11-21..2023-12-31 (tune nothing, rule is fixed) | VALIDATION 2024-01-01..2025-05-31 | OOS LOCKED 2025-06-01..2026-11-20 (touch once, at the end). Walk-forward 3y/1y rolling for stability.
leakage_risk: MA50 and sigma must use closes <= T; no centered windows; ATR from <= T; signal and fill must be separated by at least one bar.
notes: Primary candidate. Rule intentionally frozen before testing to avoid parameter mining.

hypothesis: The reversion is asymmetric: the short side (z >= +2) has materially larger net expectancy than the long side (z <= -2).
rationale: Descriptive: z<=-2 20d = -3.7 pips (n=49) vs z>=+2 20d = -189 pips (n=70). If real, a two-sided strategy is wrong and a long-only-from-highs design is right.
dv: difference in net pips per trade between sides, with CI
entry_rule: Same as H01 but evaluated on both sides; identical sizing, identical exits.
cost_assumption: identical on both sides (0.9 pip round trip) so the comparison is fair
rejection_criteria: Reject asymmetry if the bootstrap CI of the difference includes 0, or if the asymmetry disappears on validation block.
sample_requirement: >= 30 entries per side (long side only ~49 in 10y -> borderline; must report CI, not point estimate)
validation_design: Same block split as H01, evaluated jointly; permutation test with 10,000 shuffles of side labels.
leakage_risk: Low (labels known at decision time). Main risk is multiple testing across the 4 hypotheses.
notes: Cheapest test (reuses H01 code path). High false-discovery risk because it is a second look at the same data.

hypothesis: Filtering entries by volatility regime (only enter when ATR(20) is below its trailing 1-year median) improves net expectancy of H01, net of the reduced trade count.
rationale: Volatility clustering is present (|r| autocorr 0.176). Reversion amplitude scales with vol, but so does the stop distance and the risk of trend breakouts during vol spikes (e.g. 2022).
iv: binary regime flag: ATR(20) percentile vs trailing 252d
dv: net expectancy per trade and total net pips, compared with H01 unfiltered
entry_rule: H01 plus: ATR(20)_T <= median(ATR(20), last 252 bars at T)
null_hypothesis: Filtered net expectancy <= unfiltered net expectancy
rejection_criteria: Reject if filtered expectancy is not better by more than its CI, or if the improvement is only fewer trades with same per-trade result (report both).
sample_requirement: >= 25 filtered entries in-sample; report both trade-count and per-trade effects
validation_design: Paired comparison on the same dates; walk-forward stability check across 3 blocks.
leakage_risk: Median of trailing 252 bars must exclude T. Easy to accidentally include the current bar.
notes: An improvement to H01, not an independent bet. Only run after H01 is measured.

hypothesis: An exit at the measured half-life (10-15 trading days) captures most of the reversion; longer holds (30-40d) give no additional net expectancy per unit of risk.
rationale: Half-life of the MA50 deviation is 13.7d. If the process is OU-like, beyond ~2-3 half-lives the expected remaining reversion is small while exposure continues.
dv: net pips per trade and net pips per day of exposure
exit_rule: Pure time stop at h bars, no MA exit, so the horizon is identified cleanly
cost_assumption: same as H01; cost per trade constant so per-day metric is comparable
null_hypothesis: net expectancy per day of exposure is equal across horizons
rejection_criteria: Reject the half-life optimum if the 40d horizon is not worse, or if the optimum is unstable across validation blocks.
sample_requirement: same entries as H01 (~70), split across 6 horizon variants -> strong multiple-testing penalty; report all variants, not the best
validation_design: All 6 horizons reported (no cherry-picking), stability across 3 blocks.
leakage_risk: Low, but the temptation to report only the best horizon is the real risk.
notes: Highest multiple-testing risk of the four. Run last; report every variant.
